construction_notes: Throughout the paper, except Sections 5 and 6.2, values refer to the charitable tax deduction eligible for a subsidy, i.e. net of the DKK500 per-charity exemption limit: a taxpayer who donated DKK1,000 is recorded with a tax-deductible value of DKK500.
Before 2012 only total annual gifts to each eligible charity of DKK500 or more qualified for deductibility, and the first DKK500 in gifts was excluded when computing the total deduction (eq. 3).
The subsidy rate for deductible charitable contributions is one third, with slight variation by region of residence, and does not depend on the marginal tax rate.
Before 1997 charitable gifts shared a tax-return line item with a fishermen's standard deduction and a special childcare deduction, so the series starts in 1997.
Equations (1) and (2) are estimated jointly with the STATA command suest; the standard error of the ratio of the two 2008 coefficients is obtained with nlcom.
Figure 4 bins the preliminary deficit in DKK300 bins, with on average 37,000 taxpayers per bin.

Table 6 col (1): the sample is restricted to full-time workers in firms with five or more workers so that firm-occupation default contribution rates can be identified; occupations use the 2-digit ISCO classification.
Table 6 col (2): the sample is restricted to top-marginal-bracket taxpayers, classified by 2006 income, because capital pension accounts are tax-preferred only for them.

claims.statement: The 2008 introduction of third-party information reporting raised the annual growth in the number of charitable tax deductions claimed by 0.63 log points.

treatment.label: Introduction of third-party information reporting and pre-population for charitable tax deductions in Denmark in 2008

register_source.value: Danish administrative individual income-tax return data (SKAT); no Statistics Denmark register code is named

definition.value: From income year 2008 charitable organizations report contributions received from each taxpayer directly to SKAT, and SKAT uses these information reports to pre-populate charitable deductions on taxpayers' annual declarations; before 2008 charitable deductions were self-reported and verified only upon audit. In the time-series regressions the reform enters as an indicator variable for the year of the policy change, 2008.

timing.value: Income year 2008, the first year of the information reporting regime; the self-reporting regime covers 1997–2007

outcome.label: Annual growth in the number of charitable tax deductions claimed (Δ log(Number_t))

definition.value: First difference of the log of the annual number of taxpayers claiming a charitable tax deduction, 1997-2011

timing.value: Annual, income years 1998-2011 (14 growth observations)

units.value: log points of the annual change in the number of deductions claimed

magnitude.interpretation: "a 0.63 log point, or approximately 88%, increase in the number of deductions claimed", corresponding to "a 132,000 increase in the number of deductions claimed between 2007 and 2008" (p. 898-899); the abstract calls it "a doubling in the number of deductions claimed"

estimand.target_population: the population of Danish taxpayers filing a tax return; the estimate is an aggregate time-series break, not an average of individual effects
estimand.time_horizon: the first year of the information reporting regime (2008) relative to the last year of self-reporting (2007)

population.description: All Danish taxpayers claiming a charitable tax deduction, 1997-2011, aggregated to annual totals
population.selection: the annual series counts all taxpayers who claimed a charitable tax deduction; all income-tax-liable people in Denmark (about 88% of the population) must file a return

identification.source_of_variation: Interrupted time series: annual growth in the number of deductions claimed regressed on a linear time trend and an indicator for 2008, the year third-party information reporting for charitable deductions was introduced. The paper states there is no control group because the reform hit all taxpayers at once.

key_assumptions.assumption: No other policy change or contemporaneous shock in 2008 could account for the surge in charitable deductions claimed
key_assumptions.supported_by: Footnote 14: the authors state they are unaware of any other policy change occurring at the same time

key_assumptions.assumption: Absent the reform the outcome would have continued along the estimated linear time trend
key_assumptions.supported_by: The pre-reform change is several orders of magnitude smaller than the 2007-2008 change (Fig. 1a, 1b); the 2006 and 2007 claim distributions are almost identical (Fig. 2)

key_assumptions.assumption: The reform changed reporting behaviour only, not actual charitable giving behaviour
key_assumptions.supported_by: Administrative annual reports filed with SKAT by the 25 largest charities show almost unchanged growth in the number and value of donations around 2008 (Fig. 3)

threats_discussed: the policy change affected all taxpayers at the same time, so there is no control group
the reform might have coincided with, or caused, a change in actual giving behaviour rather than reporting
a relaxation of the upper eligibility threshold for regular gifts in 2007 (DKK6,600 to DKK13,600) and a further modest rise in 2008 affects the upper tail of the claim distribution
married couples might have reported deductions jointly pre-reform and individually post-reform
robustness_checks: a quadratic time trend added to eqs (1) and (2) leaves the coefficients on the 2008 indicator essentially unchanged, and the quadratic term is insignificant (footnote 15)
a version of Fig. 1b grouping the donations of married couples together is qualitatively unchanged (footnote 13)
the 2006 and 2007 pre-reform claim distributions, and the 2008 and 2009 post-reform distributions, are almost identical (Fig. 2)
administrative reports filed by the 25 largest charities show no break in the number or value of donations around 2008 (Fig. 3)

estimator.value: OLS time-series regression with heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors

estimation.specification: Equation (1): annual log change in the number of deductions on a constant, a linear time trend and an indicator for 2008

mediators_claimed: previously unclaimed (self-reported but omitted) charitable deductions becoming pre-populated

heterogeneity.finding: almost a 10-fold increase in claims below DKK500 and a more than doubling in the DKK500-1,500 range, but little change above DKK3,000 (Fig. 1b)

heterogeneity.dimension: accountants versus the rest of the population
heterogeneity.finding: no evidence of a break in trend among accountants for deductions larger than DKK500 (Fig. 6b)

ambiguities: The paper prints no stars, p-value or confidence interval for eq. (1); statistically_significant=true is inferred from the printed coefficient and its standard error (recorded as derivation e14).
Equation (1) is not an exhibit in the digest, so source_table_id is null.
The strategy is coded 'other' (interrupted time series): the paper explicitly says it has no control group and calls the estimate approximate.
